drivingQuestion: Does a live full-term fetus found in a slaughtered animal require its own slaughter, or does its mother's slaughter render it permitted?
outcomeNote: A mishna recording a three-way tannaitic dispute; no resolution is offered within the unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה, וּמָצָא בָּהּ בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה חַי אוֹ מֵת, אוֹ בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה מֵת – קוֹרְעוֹ וּמוֹצִיא אֶת דָּמוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who slaughtered an animal and found within it an eight-»month«-old» fetus, i.e., one that was not full term, whether it was «alive or dead, or a nine-»month«-old» fetus, i.e., one that was full term, that was «dead,» that fetus is permitted by virtue of the slaughter of its mother, as it is considered part of its mother. Therefore, its blood is considered part of its mother’s blood and is prohibited, so one must «tear» the fetus «and remove its blood» before it may be consumed.

segments.he: מָצָא בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה חַי – טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה, וְחַיָּיב בְּ״אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: שְׁחִיטַת אִמּוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ.
segments.en: If «he found» within it «a live nine-»month«-old» fetus, «it requires» its own «slaughter,» as it is considered an independent full-fledged animal, «and» if one slaughters both the mother and fetus on the same day, «one is liable for» violating the prohibition against slaughtering an animal «itself and its offspring» on the same day; this is «the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say:» Even when the fetus is nine months old, it is still considered part of its mother, and «the slaughter of its mother renders it permitted» for consumption.

segments.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֵׁזוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בֶּן חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְחוֹרֵשׁ בַּשָּׂדֶה – שְׁחִיטַת אִמּוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ. קְרָעָהּ וּמָצָא בָּהּ בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה חַי – טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה, לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁחֲטָה אִמּוֹ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Shimon Shezuri says: Even» if the fetus emerged alive and «is» now «five years old and plowing in the field,» the earlier «slaughter of its mother rendered it permitted» and it does not require slaughter before it is eaten. But if «one tore» an animal, i.e., he killed it without slaughtering it, «and» inside «he found a live nine-»month«-old» fetus, everyone agrees that the fetus «requires» its own «slaughter because its mother was not slaughtered.»

moves.cueHe: השוחט את הבהמה, ומצא בה בן שמנה חי או מת
moves.summary: an eight-month fetus alive or dead, or a dead nine-month fetus, is permitted by the mother's slaughter and is torn open to drain its blood

moves.cueHe: מצא בן תשעה חי – טעון שחיטה, וחייב ב״אותו ואת בנו״
moves.summary: R' Meir rules that a live full-term fetus needs its own slaughter and counts for the אותו ואת בנו prohibition
moves.about: whether a live nine-month-old fetus found in a properly slaughtered animal requires its own slaughter, or is rendered permitted by its mother's slaughter

moves.summary: the Sages rule that the mother's slaughter permits even a live full-term fetus

moves.cueHe: רבי שמעון שזורי אומר: אפילו בן חמש שנים וחורש בשדה
moves.summary: R' Shimon Shezuri extends the permission conferred by the mother's slaughter to the animal even years after it has grown
moves.about: whether a live nine-month-old fetus ever requires its own slaughter — R' Shimon Shezuri holds its mother's slaughter permits it even years later, R' Meir that it requires slaughter

moves.cueHe: קרעה ומצא בה בן תשעה חי – טעון שחיטה
moves.summary: where the mother was torn open rather than slaughtered, all agree the live full-term fetus requires its own slaughter

edges.cueHe: דברי רבי מאיר. וחכמים אומרים: שחיטת אמו מטהרתו
